prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1288; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a parking lot collision with a knee injury reported by the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney. Initial contact made and claim file opened for review.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and spoke with two witnesses, who both confirm the vehicles made contact in the parking lot as the claimant described. Photos taken at the scene are on file.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, whose account of the impact matches the claimant's description. The damage shown in the photos lines up with the reported point of impact.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver involved is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates coverage.

Entry 5: Claimant described the knee injury and how it happened during a recorded call. The account was consistent with the police report and the witness statements already on file.

Entry 6: Reviewed the vehicle appraisal. The damage pattern fits the impact described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the inspection notes.

Entry 7: Obtained medical records showing the knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of this type. No prior injury to the same knee or area appears in the claimant's history.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with pain and mobility improving steadily, and the provider noted that care is tapering as recovery progresses. Claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Reviewed the file as a whole. Witnesses, photos, the other driver, and the police report all support the accident as described, and the claimant's presence in the vehicle is confirmed. Claim is progressing through standard evaluation.
